scholarships.title: Doctoral Recruitment Call 2026 - Social Sciences, Humanities & Cultural Studies (SSH Call 2026), University of Vienna

existing.funding_period: per month gross, paid 14 times per year
existing.description: The University of Vienna's SSH Call 2026 is a central recruitment call offering at least 40 fully funded four-year doctoral positions in the social sciences, humanities and cultural studies across nine participating doctoral schools, including the Vienna Doctoral School in Cognition, Behavior, and Neuroscience (CoBeNe). Positions are 30 hours per week under collective bargaining agreement §48 VwGr. B1, paid at a monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10 paid 14 times per year, and employees are exempt from tuition fees. Applications for the 2026 round ran from 7 January to 2 March 2026 at 14:00 CET through the University of Vienna PhD Selection Tool, with employment starting between 1 July and 1 October 2026. The University runs a central doctoral call annually, so the next cycle is expected but its dates were not yet published on the verification date.
eligibility: Highly qualified graduate who will have completed a Diploma or Master's degree by 30 June 2026 in a field covered by one of the participating doctoral schools or a closely related discipline
Demonstrates a strong interest in academic research and in pursuing a PhD at the University of Vienna
Can clearly assign the proposed dissertation project to the research focus of one of the participating doctoral schools
Able to take up the doctoral position between 1 July and 1 October 2026
Meets the doctoral admission requirements of the University of Vienna by the start of employment
Already enrolled applicants are eligible if their first doctoral enrolment at the University of Vienna was in winter semester 2025/26 or later
existing.eligibility_summary: Highly qualified graduates who complete a Diploma or Master's degree by 30 June 2026 in a field covered by a participating doctoral school, can align their project to that school's research focus, and can take up the position between 1 July and 1 October 2026.
benefits: Monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10 in salary group B1 for 30 hours per week, paid 14 times per year
Comprehensive social security coverage, with health insurance also covering family members and unemployed partners
A workspace provided at the university
Entitlement to parental leave under Austrian employment law
Possibility of teaching duties under the collective bargaining agreement
coverage: Salaried employment of 30 hours per week for four years under collective bargaining agreement §48 VwGr. B1
Exemption from University of Vienna tuition fees for employees
Comprehensive social security coverage including health insurance for family members and unemployed partners, pension and unemployment insurance
requirements: A separate CV is not required, because all relevant information is captured in the structured fields of the online application form
Only one application may be submitted; if more are submitted, only the last one is considered
No confirmation of supervision is required at the application stage, and supervisors should not be contacted for that purpose
Applicants who already hold external funding for the doctoral project or an existing praedoc-level employment contract of at least two years cannot receive funding through this call
Non-EU/EEA applicants must obtain the required visa or work permit themselves
Funding through the SSH Call cannot be extended beyond four years
documents: Research proposal of a maximum of 5 pages including bibliography (PDF)
Master, Bachelor and/or Diploma degree certificates and transcript of records or diploma supplements (PDF)
Official identification document, passport or ID card, for enrolment (PDF)
If applicable and available: residence permit and language certificates (PDF)
Writing sample, for example a chapter of the Master's thesis or a published article, for certain named doctoral schools (PDF)
Contact details of two referees; no letters of recommendation are submitted at the application stage
existing.english_requirement: All doctoral schools accept applications in English. A prerequisite for admission to the doctoral programme is usually German and/or English proficiency at level C1; language certificates are not mandatory for most subjects, but candidates are asked to provide any certificate available.
application_method: Central online application through the University of Vienna PhD Selection Tool
A u:account must be registered first if the applicant does not already have one
existing.selection_notes: Candidates are assessed on academic achievements, previous research experience, the quality and feasibility of the research proposal, and the fit between the project and the participating doctoral schools. Applications are reviewed by University of Vienna researchers including potential supervisors. Formal eligibility checks take place in March, interviews are held online between late March and mid-May, and final decisions are expected by June. A ranked waiting list is created, and candidates have two weeks to accept an offer.
existing.best_fit: Graduates in the social sciences, humanities, law, cultural studies, theology, philosophy and the participating interdisciplinary doctoral schools who will complete their degree by 30 June 2026 and can start between July and October.
existing.notes: Nine doctoral schools participated in the SSH Call 2026: Advanced Research School in Law and Jurisprudence (Ars Iuris Vienna); Doctoral School of Philological and Cultural Studies (PhilKult); Vienna Doctoral School in Cognition, Behavior, and Neuroscience (CoBeNe); Vienna Doctoral School of Education (DSE); Vienna Doctoral School of Historical and Cultural Studies (DSHCS); Vienna Doctoral School of Philosophy (VDP); Vienna Doctoral School of Social Sciences (ViDSS); Vienna Doctoral School of Theology and Research on Religion (VDTR); Vienna International School in Earth and Space Sciences (VISESS). Additional funding or travel support has to be discussed with the institute and supervisors at the start of employment.
existing.application_period: The 2026 round ran 7 January to 2 March 2026 at 14:00 CET. The University of Vienna announces a new central doctoral call each year, so the next application window must be confirmed on the careers site.
existing.deadline_display: "Application period: 7 January – 2 March 2026, 14:00 CET" for the 2026 round; the University runs an annual central call and had not published the next window on 2026-10-04.
existing.program_type: Central annual recruitment call for salaried predoctoral (Praedoc) positions at a doctoral school

scholarships.title: Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide
scholarships.official_source: OeAD-GmbH – Austria's Agency for Education and Internationalisation

existing.description: The Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide finances short research stays in Austria for young researchers from all disciplines and all countries except Austria. The published grant benefit is a supplementary monthly grant of EUR 1,300, together with assistance in arranging accommodation and health insurance, but scholarship holders pay the costs of accommodation and insurance themselves and must show own funds. Tuition fees at Austrian public universities and universities of applied sciences do not have to be paid by grant holders, and may be waived upon request to the rectorate, but this does not apply to private universities and private colleges. Holders from listed non-European developing countries also receive a travel costs subsidy of up to EUR 1,200 upon submission of original travel invoices.
eligibility: Eligible for application are: a. Postgraduates pursuing a doctoral/PhD programme outside of Austria; b. Postgraduates and postdocs wishing to pursue research in Austria with a view to an academic career and who completed their studies (at a university outside of Austria) after 30 September 2025; c. Postdocs who are working as researchers at a university outside of Austria
Applicants must not have lived/studied/pursued research/pursued academic work in Austria in the last six months before taking up the grant
Applicants who have completed their academic education mainly in Austria (does not apply to applications by Postdocs) or who are already permanently residing in Austria are not eligible to apply
Maximum age: 35 years (born on or after 01 October 1991)
Country of origin: all except Austria
Language skills: very good knowledge of English and/or German
Consent of a lecturer at the Austrian target university to supervise the applicant academically is a required document
The scholarship will only be granted for projects that can be completed within the scholarship period (max. 9 months)
existing.eligibility_summary: Young researchers from countries other than Austria, aged 35 or under at the start of the stay, who are pursuing a PhD outside Austria or who completed their studies abroad after 30 September 2025, and who have a written supervision confirmation from an Austrian university lecturer.
benefits: Assistance in arranging accommodation (OeAD student housing may be applied for; availability is limited and a room cannot be guaranteed)
The OeAD can help with taking out health insurance accepted by the Austrian authorities
coverage: Assistance in arranging accommodation and health insurance (scholarship holders have to pay the costs for accommodation and insurance themselves)

Grant holders do not have to pay tuition fees in Austria; tuition fees may be waived upon request to the Rectorate of the public university or university college of teacher education for the semesters in which studies or research can be shown to have been completed elsewhere, i.e. as part of transnational EU, state or university mobility programmes; any tuition fees at universities of applied sciences may be waived by the rectorate upon application

Scholarship holders with citizenship and travel from non-European developing countries (Least Developed Countries, Low Income Countries and Lower Middle Income Countries and Territories according to the DAC list, plus Gabon, Malaysia, Namibia, South Africa, Thailand) or for their return will also receive a travel costs subsidy of up to 1,200 Euro upon submission of original travel invoices
requirements: The documents have to be uploaded with the online application at www.scholarships.at
The use of generative AI must be indicated in the application
Applicants who seek admission to a university in Austria have to contact the institution of their choice directly
Grant holders must be continuously present at their place of study in Austria to study or conduct their research project

Scholarship holders are not allowed to engage in gainful employment. Exempt is marginal employment within research/the Arts at universities, universities of applied sciences and research institutions in compliance with residence laws and employment laws for foreign nationals (in 2026: 551.10 Euro per month)
The grant has to be consumed by the end of 2028
Scholarship holders are obliged to submit a final report at the end of their scholarship stay
It is strongly recommended that you take out adequate health, accident and repatriation insurance valid at your destination; the scholarship holder is responsible for taking out insurance
documents: Two letters of recommendation by university lecturers
Consent of a lecturer at the Austrian target university to supervise the applicant academically
Scanned copy of your passport (page with the name and photo)
Scanned copy of your university graduation certificate of your diploma, master, PhD or doctoral studies
Only for PhD-students: confirmation that proves your participation in a PhD-programme at your home university
Only for postdocs: confirmation that proves your employment at your home university
existing.english_requirement: Language skills: very good knowledge of English and/or German. No official testing certificate such as TOEFL is needed, but you should have sufficient knowledge of English in the respective subject area, and your Austrian academic supervisor also has to confirm that your project can be done in English.
application_method: Secure a written confirmation of supervision from a lecturer at the Austrian target university using the OeAD template

Obtain two letters of recommendation from university lecturers with letterhead, date, signature and the stamp of the university/department; letters must not be older than six months at the time of application
Prepare the passport scan (page with name and photo), the graduation certificate scan, and the additional confirmation for PhD students or postdocs
Fill in all sections of the online application at www.scholarships.at thoroughly, observing the minimum number of words; no separate research proposal upload is needed
Upload all documents and press submit before 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET
Await the expert evaluation; results are expected at the beginning of July 2027
existing.selection_notes: The selection follows a multistage process: 1. Examination of the formal requirements; 2. Examination of the application's general plausibility; 3. Assessment and evaluation of the application by experts; 4. Final decision by the BMFWF. Incomplete applications and applications not complying with the application criteria will not be accepted for the further selection process. All formally valid applications are then evaluated by experts from the respective field and the selection committee awards the best applicants. The selection is competitive, i.e. there is no legal claim to a grant even if all application requirements are fulfilled; the number of grants awarded during one call depends on the quota and/or the available budget.
existing.best_fit: Postgraduates enrolled in a doctoral/PhD programme outside Austria, postgraduates and postdocs who completed their studies at a university outside Austria after 30 September 2025 and want to pursue research in Austria with a view to an academic career, and postdocs working as researchers at a university outside Austria, all aged 35 or under at the start of the stay.
existing.notes: Grant period is 1 to 9 months and must be consumed by the end of 2028. Extensions are not possible for this grant. The earliest possible start is September 2027 (the Austrian academic year 2027/28). Stay dates must consist of full months only, starting on the first of a month and ending on the last; short-term grants of 1 month should be consumed in February or September. Applicants must have interrupted any stay in Austria for at least six months before taking up the grant. Gainful employment is not allowed, with a marginal employment exemption of EUR 551.10 per month in 2026. A final report is obligatory at the end of the stay. The grant contract (Letter of Award and Letter of Acceptance) defines start and end date, grant amount, payment modalities, compulsory attendance at the guest institution, performance report and final report, data protection and repayment obligations. The grant cannot be used to enrol in a Master or PhD programme in Austria. Without written proof of accommodation in Austria, a residence permit is not granted. Applicants from non-EU/EEA countries planning a stay of more than 6 months whose accommodation costs exceed EUR 386.43/month may need to prove additional funds to the Austrian residence authority.
existing.application_period: Online application open from September 2026 and closing 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET, for research stays during the Austrian academic year 2027/28 (starting September 2027). Expert evaluation takes place after the deadline; results are expected to be published at the beginning of July 2027.
existing.deadline_display: Closing date for applications: 01.12.2026. Online application is possible from September to December 1st; the application deadline for this grant is December 1st, 2026, 23:59 (CET) for all applications for stays during the academic year 2027/28.
